intro: Use this guide to score the Lead Machine against the 100-point rubric; 80 wins. Every mark needs evidence: the 12-lead test report, Zap history, the Leads sheet and the demo. Different designs are fine if the results match the brief.

rows.full: 11 or 12 of the 12 test leads land in the expected tier (e.g. lead 9's ₦1.5m monthly becomes about 346,000 weekly and scores warm 6; lead 11 scores 5 with no budget), and lead 8 shows Filtered in Zap history with no Leads row.
rows.partial: 8–10 leads correct, usually monthly budgets left unconverted, Agbowo or Ogbomoso treated as inside the zone, or the test lead saved as cold instead of filtered.
rows.low: Fewer than 8 correct, tiers guessed by the AI instead of calculated by code, or no test report.

rows.full: Intake starts from Catch Raw Hook (instant); Zap history timestamps show acknowledgements within 15 minutes and hot alerts within 5 for every test lead.
rows.partial: Emails arrive within 15 minutes but the hot alert depends on a polling step or a sheet trigger, so some alerts take longer than 5 minutes.
rows.low: Intake polls a sheet or form, or timings aren't shown.

rows.full: Warm leads get exactly one follow-up after the 3-day delay; a warm lead that replied (status Replied via Zap 2) gets none; status moves Contacted → Followed up and followed_up_at is filled.
rows.partial: The follow-up sends, but there's no re-check of status after the delay, or replied leads were never tested.
rows.low: No follow-up, follow-ups to hot or cold leads, or more than one per lead.

rows.full: Every lead has a Leads row with lead_id, received_at, a numeric weekly_budget, score, tier and status from the dropdowns; contacted_at and status update as emails go out and replies come in.
rows.partial: Rows exist but budgets are text, statuses never change from New, or dates are in mixed formats.
rows.low: Leads missing from the sheet, or one free-text column holding everything.

rows.full: No automatic email mentions a price or discount; spam and test leads receive nothing; the hook URL and any token or keys are kept out of screenshots, the sheet and the video.
rows.partial: One email template edges towards a promise ("special rates"), or spam gets a polite reply.
rows.low: Prices or discounts in automatic emails, spam emailed back, or keys or the hook URL visible in evidence.

rows.full: All three curveballs handled and shown: monthly and missing budgets (÷ 4.33, empty → 0); a Settings tab (or similar) switches alert_to and caller_name with one cell edit; a duplicate-email check and honeypot stop a 40-lead flood before AI and email tasks.
rows.partial: Two curveballs handled, or the Tolu-away change hard-coded into the Zap instead of being switchable.

rows.full: A test report with expected vs actual tier, emails, alerts and tasks per lead for all 12; a monthly estimate at 60 leads under about 500 tasks, built from Zap history; a video of about two minutes showing a hot lead, its email, alert and Leads row.
rows.partial: Report or estimate incomplete (no tasks per lead, guessed numbers) or the video runs long or skips the alert.
rows.low: No report, no estimate, or no video.

evidence: The Leads sheet (test data only) with the 12 test leads, showing score, tier, status and dates.
The AI extraction spec: prompt, typed output fields and its results on the 12 leads.
The scoring Code step and a screenshot of its output for at least two leads.
Screenshots of Zap 1 (with Paths), Zap 2 and the warm follow-up steps, hook URL hidden.
Zap history screenshots: one per tier, the filtered test lead, and a replied lead skipped at follow-up.
The test report table: expected vs actual tier, emails, alerts and tasks per lead, plus the monthly task estimate.
Short notes and screenshots showing how each curveball was handled.
A two-minute screen recording of a hot lead going through end to end.
mistakes: Letting the AI decide the tier instead of extracting fields and scoring with code.
Not converting monthly budgets or crashing on empty budgets.
Follow-up with no status re-check after the delay, so leads who replied still get chased.
Spam or the test lead receiving an acknowledgement email.
Task estimate guessed, or the duplicate check placed after the AI step so a flood still burns tasks.
The hook URL, token or real contact details visible in screenshots or the demo.
